intro: True to the vision of its creator Michel Etevenon, the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe 2026 stands out more than ever as the benchmark solo transatlantic race, a symbol of absolute freedom, ocean adventure, and the ultimate challenge. Every four years, skippers leave Saint-Malo for a crossing of the North Atlantic to Guadeloupe, facing depressions, trade winds, and the vastness of the ocean alone in a race that has become legendary in the world of sailing.

True to its DNA of openness and innovation, the event will welcome two Vintage classes this year, monohulls and multihulls, replacing the former Rhum categories. These new divisions celebrate the return of legendary boats that have marked the history of offshore racing and encourage the reuse of existing vessels, even those outside the professional class rating system. They thus offer a second life to ocean-going machines designed for solo transatlantic crossings, perpetuating the pioneering spirit of great maritime adventures.

For its 13<sup>th</sup> edition, the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe will once again bring together, at the starting line in Saint-Malo, one of the most prestigious fleets in ocean sailing: Ultim trimarans, high-tech multihulls, racing monohulls, and exceptional sailboats. Between extreme performance, weather strategy, and human endurance, this transatlantic race remains, for sailors and spectators alike, a lifelong dream, an extraordinary crossing where one of the greatest challenges in world sailing unfolds, sailed solo.

classes.intro:
The ULTIM Class aims to push the boundaries of technology and performance in offshore racing. It unites owners, teams and sailors driven by the quest for speed and innovation, propelled solely by wind power.

True floating laboratories, the maxi-multihulls ULTIM embody exceptional expertise and actively contribute to the advancement of knowledge.

Through extraordinary sporting challenges, the ULTIM Class embodies a pioneering spirit of audacity, adventure and freedom, resolutely focused on the future.
classes.description:
An ULTIM is a giant of the seas, designed to go faster, farther, and stronger. These 32-meter maxi-multihulls, among the fastest sailboats ever built, are capable of crossing oceans at speeds once reserved for motorized vessels, propelled solely by the wind. True technological marvels, ULTIMs literally fly above the water thanks to their foils, large submerged wings that lift the hull and reduce drag. On board, every element is optimized for performance: cutting-edge composite materials, sophisticated onboard systems, and an extreme architecture designed to withstand the most violent conditions on the planet. Designed for long solo or short-handed voyages, these exceptional trimarans are both record-breaking machines and tools for exploration. They allow sailors to push human and technical boundaries, while paving the way for tomorrow's innovations in the maritime sector.
Spectacular, powerful and elegant, the ULTIMs embody the avant-garde of offshore racing: a subtle balance between audacity, precision and mastery, where every mile covered writes a little more of the history of speed sailing.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: A giant carbon mast, over 35 meters tall, one of the tallest in the world for offshore racing. It supports sails of over 300 m² and must withstand the extreme stresses of foils.

points.label: DAGGERBOARD
points.detail: Integrated daggerboards in the central hull, retractable depending on the point of sail. They ensure heading and limit lateral drift when the boat is flying on its foils or sailing upwind.

points.label: FOILS
points.detail: Retractable foils several meters long, integrated into the connecting arms. They lift the entire boat out of the water, eliminating hull drag and allowing it to exceed 50 knots.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: Rudders positioned at the rear of the central hull, two in number. They provide steering at very high speed and can be partially raised to optimize performance.

points.label: COCKPIT
points.detail: Ultra-protected cockpit within the central hull, designed for solo sailing at very high speeds. Equipped with navigation and hydraulic appendage control systems.

points.label: SAILS
points.detail: An exceptional sail plan exceeding 300 m² with all sails set. The combination of mainsail and giant gennaker propels the Ultim to over 40 knots downwind.

classes.intro:
The Ocean Fifty class, created in 2021, is a continuation of the Multi50 class, whose history is deeply linked to that of offshore racing.

For more than fifteen years, this fleet has constantly evolved. It reached a decisive milestone with its professionalization in 2015, then with the adoption of foils in 2017. In 2021, it officially took the name Ocean Fifty, marking a new stage in its development.

Now fully mature, the class relies on a structured sporting program built around an annual championship, the Ocean Fifty Series, complemented by a major transatlantic crossing. This versatile calendar rewards both consistency and commitment: close-quarters regattas where precise maneuvers, quality starts, and tactical finesse make all the difference, followed by an ocean race where tactics give way to long-term strategy.

Dynamic and responsible, the Ocean Fifty class ensures that rules are maintained to guarantee controlled budgets, compatible with the commitment of SMEs, while ensuring a high level of performance and the long-term sustainability of the value of the boats.
classes.description:
An Ocean Fifty is a 50-foot (approximately 15.24 m) offshore racing trimaran designed for high speeds, whether sailed single-handed or with a crew. It's a pure racing machine, but on a more manageable scale compared to the giant ULTIM trimarans.
These boats have three hulls: a central hull and two lateral floats connected by arms. This design offers lightness, stability, and power. Since the advent of foils, submerged wings that partially lift the boat, they can literally "fly" above the water, reducing drag and significantly increasing speed. An Ocean Fifty can exceed 35 to 40 knots (approximately 65 to 75 km/h), but its true strength isn't its top speed: it's its ability to maintain very high speeds for extended periods, even in rough seas. On the ocean, the swell is a capricious tyrant, and these trimarans are designed to negotiate with it rather than fight it head-on. It is an “accessible” offshore racing platform: fast, demanding, tactical, and robust enough to face the Atlantic.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: A slender carbon mast of approximately 26 meters positioned on the central axis of the trimaran. Designed for offshore multihull sailing, it supports sails of over 200 m².

points.label: DAGGERBOARD
points.detail: Retractable daggerboards integrated into the floats or central hull. They ensure heading and resistance to lateral drift, and are adjusted according to the point of sail to optimize performance.

points.label: FOILS
points.detail: L-shaped or C-shaped foils integrated into the floats. These allow the trimaran to partially fly out of the water, reducing hull drag and achieving top speeds exceeding 35 knots.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: Twin rudders positioned at the rear of the central hull. Optimized for high-speed navigation, they ensure the trimaran's maneuverability both in coastal regattas and transatlantic crossings.

points.label: COCKPIT
points.detail: Pilot station positioned on the central hull, designed for solo or short-handed sailing. Centralized access to winches, halyards and appendage adjustment systems.

points.label: SAILS
points.detail: Generous sail area, up to 250 m² downwind with the gennaker deployed. Mainsail, genoa and lighter sails allow for optimal speed on all points of sail.

classes.intro:
The Class40 association brings together the skippers of Class40 boats as well as all those interested in the development and promotion of these sailboats.

The class aims to bring together experienced amateur sailors and professional skippers around a calendar of coastal and ocean races, in a spirit of conviviality, mutual support and sharing of experience.

Its appeal lies in particular in a simple and rigorous gauge, guaranteeing high performance while maintaining controlled budgets.
classes.description: A Class40 is a 40-foot (12.20 m) offshore racing monohull designed for fast, long-distance, and reliable sailing on major ocean routes. Recognizable by its wide, powerful hull, clean deck, and protected cockpit, it is optimized for performance whether sailing solo or double-handed. Without lifting foils, the Class40 prioritizes robustness, simplicity, and efficiency. Its speed comes from its planing hull, capable of surfing waves for extended periods, and a generous sail plan perfectly suited to long passages. Fast, seaworthy, and demanding, the Class40 is now one of the most dynamic classes in offshore racing and the most represented in the fleet of this 13<sup>th</sup> edition. It offers a unique balance between performance, accessibility, and ocean adventure.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: Carbon or composite mast of approximately 19 meters, standardized by the Class40 rule. Masthead rig with forestay for the genoa. Fixed mast: canting masts are prohibited by the rule.

points.label: KEEL
points.detail: Fixed, weighted keel required by the class rules: canting keels are prohibited. It ensures the stability and anti-drift action of the monohull during ocean crossings.

points.label: BOW
points.detail: The bow of the boat is optimized for wave penetration. On modern Class40s (Scow), the bow is widened and flattened to maximize lift and improve downwind performance.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: Two fixed rudders positioned in a V at the rear of the hull. They ensure steering and directional stability, optimized for solo navigation over long ocean distances.

points.label: COCKPIT
points.detail: Secure cockpit with high lifelines and regulated safety systems, designed for solo or double-handed sailing. Quick access to winches and maneuvers from a compact space.

points.label: SAILS
points.detail: Sail area limited to 115 m² by the rating rules. Battened mainsail, genoa, jib and gennaker make up the arsenal of the Class40, adapted to all conditions of offshore racing.

classes.intro:
The IMOCA class comprises 60-foot (18.28 m) ocean-going monohulls. In this 13th edition of the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe, 25 sailors from the class will be competing! IMOCA boats are the same ones that participate in the Vendée Globe and are considered to be constantly evolving machines.

The class showcases over 30 years of technological innovation: keels, sail plans, cockpits, coachroofs, and foils, which constantly stimulate the creativity of naval architects and sailors. Even though they are bound by a class rule that limits length, beam, and the number of appendages and sails, for example, IMOCA boats nevertheless allow considerable freedom to architects and sailors. Thus, these boats and their skippers are ready to face the extreme and harshest conditions on all oceans. This is evidenced by the presence of the world's best sailors in this class, determined to compete in the ocean sprint that is the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe.
classes.description:
An IMOCA (International Monohull Open Class Association) is a 60-foot (18.28 m) monohull ocean racing sailboat designed for single-handed or short-crewed sailing.
These boats are specifically developed for major offshore races such as the Vendée Globe or the Route du Rhum.
They are built from very lightweight and strong composite materials, primarily carbon fiber.
Since the 2010s, most IMOCAs have been equipped with foils, lateral appendages that partially lift the hull to increase speed.
An IMOCA can regularly exceed 35 knots (approximately 64.3 km/h) in good conditions.
The class is considered "open": designers can innovate, but within a framework of strict rules guaranteeing safety and fairness.
Each boat is designed as a unique prototype, incorporating the most advanced technologies in naval architecture. Reliability is essential, as these sailboats face the oceans alone for days, weeks, or months.
The skippers live aboard in a minimalist space, optimized for performance rather than comfort.
These boats represent the pinnacle of solo offshore racing, combining technology, human endurance, and strategy.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: A carbon mast of approximately 28 meters, among the largest on racing monohulls. Designed to withstand the extreme conditions of the open ocean.

points.label: KEEL
points.detail: With a maximum length of 4.5 m, its weight is between 2.2 T and 2.85 T. The keel can be canted up to 38° to optimize stability according to the point of sail and sea conditions.

points.label: FOILS
points.detail: Retractable side appendages allow the hull to be partially lifted out of the water. They reduce drag and propel the IMOCA to speeds exceeding 35 knots in good conditions.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: There are two of them, positioned at the rear on each side of the hull. They are used to steer the boat and can be raised if necessary to reduce drag.

points.label: COCKPIT
points.detail: Reserved for maneuvers and adjustments, this is the area from which the skipper pilots the boat. Depending on the model, the cockpit can be fully enclosed (roof) or partially open.

points.label: SAILS
points.detail: An impressive sail plan that can exceed 300 m² with all sails set. Mainsail, genoa, gennaker and code 0 allow for optimal propulsion on all points of sail.

classes.intro:
Vintage Monohulls are classic monohulls that have left their mark on the history of offshore racing. Robust and authentic, they bear witness to an era when ingenuity took precedence over technology, and when the sailor made the difference against the elements.

These legendary sailboats have participated in the major editions of the Route du Rhum since its inception. Built from fiberglass, aluminum, or marine plywood, they offer a challenging sailing experience in the purest tradition of great ocean raids. To see them take the start alongside modern machines is to witness the history of sailing in motion.
classes.description: Vintage Monohulls are classic monohulls that have left their mark on the history of offshore racing. Robust and authentic, they offer a challenging sailing experience in the purest tradition of great ocean raids. These boats bear witness to an era when ingenuity took precedence over technology.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: The characteristic aluminum mast of classic monohulls, rigged at the masthead to maximize sail area. Robust and proven, it withstands offshore conditions.

points.label: KEEL
points.detail: Fixed keel ballasted in lead or cast iron. Ensures lateral stability and compensates for heeling under sail. Typical weight between 1 and 2 tonnes depending on the size of the boat.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: Single or double rudder positioned at the rear of the hull. On vintage monohulls, the rudder is often suspended or integrated into the sternpost, operated by tiller or wheel.

points.label: COCKPIT
points.detail: Open central navigation area, designed for crewed or solo sailing. Main living space during long ocean crossings.

classes.intro:
Vintage Multi boats are historic multihulls that revolutionized offshore racing. Legendary catamarans and trimarans, they embody the audacity of the pioneers who dared to bet on speed and lightness to cross the oceans.

These exceptional boats bear witness to an era when ingenuity took precedence over resources. Before foils and ultra-technical materials, naval architects and sailors were already pushing the boundaries with sleek multihulls, often handcrafted. Sailing a Vintage Multi today is to reconnect with the history of competitive sailing.
classes.description: Vintage Multi boats are historic multihulls that revolutionized offshore racing by introducing speed and lightness to long-distance crossings. Legendary catamarans and trimarans, they embody the audacity of the pioneers who dared to rely on multiple hulls.

points.label: MAST
points.detail: Carbon or aluminum mast positioned on the central axis of the multihull, rigged at the masthead with forestay and lateral shrouds. Its height often exceeds 20 meters on the largest vessels.

points.label: DAGGERBOARD
points.detail: A fixed or retractable hydrodynamic appendage that ensures heading and limits lateral drift under sail. On vintage multihulls, daggerboards are often large surfaces made of aluminum or laminate.

points.label: RUDDERS
points.detail: Rudders are positioned at the rear of each hull or float. On vintage multihulls, there are often two or four of them, used to steer the entire structure.
